stimuli.description: A wooden box (94 cm long; 30 cm wide; 11.5 cm deep) divided into a nest-box, entrance chamber, and two electric boxes (one white, one black). Electric shock was delivered via wires on the floor of the black box. Visual discrimination difficulty was manipulated by varying the brightness difference between the white and black boxes.
stimuli.source: Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and text on pages 460-461

limitations: The irregularity of curve II (for easy discrimination) at 375 units of stimulus strength is attributed to small sample sizes.
The conclusion regarding the optimal stimulus for easy discrimination is presented tentatively, subject to future research, as animals were not subjected to injurious stimulation.
Only three strengths of stimulus were used for experiments of set I, making it possible that the most favorable strength was not discovered, which slightly weakens conclusion 5.
The conclusions are based on the study of mice alone, and the authors plan to repeat experiments with other animals.
The method of controlling visual conditions using cardboards was less accurate and describable compared to alternative methods (e.g., using screens to control light amount).
